STX.thesis_one_line: Hard-drive maker whose AI-storage boom is real, but the stock already needs a decade of ~22% yearly cash-flow growth to be worth today's price.
kill_criteria: Guidance beat-margin compresses to <3% (vs the ~4-14% beats of the last three quarters) for two consecutive quarters
Sequential revenue growth turns negative for two consecutive quarters (vs the +7-24% sequential growth of the last four quarters)
Net debt/EBITDA rises above 1.5x (currently well under 0.5x)
Any BIS finding of non-compliance with the April 2023 Settlement Agreement
Nearline $/TB pricing (company-disclosed or via WDC read-across) declines quarter-over-quarter
key_adverse_facts: April 2023 BIS Settlement Agreement over Huawei HDD export violations: $300m penalty, quarterly $15m installments through ~2028; $120m still accrued as of 3 Jul 2026; non-compliance could lift a suspended denial order restricting exports
Securities class action (class period Sep 2020-Apr 2023) settled in principle Apr 2026 for $175m ($105m company charge); final court approval hearing 2026-11-17
Federal Circuit vacated a 2022 district-court win for Seagate in the Lambeth Magnetic Structures patent case (Sep 2025), remanding for a new trial
Stock's own 10-K performance graph shows a >990% five-year total return (Jul 2021-Jul 2026) vs S&P 500's +87.6% - an extreme re-rating on a historically cyclical hardware business
d4/Yahoo quant snapshot's trailing FCF figure ($1.94bn) is stale vs the FY2026 10-K's actual $3.1bn FCF, understating the true FCF yield by roughly 60%
data_conflicts: d4_live_snapshot fcf_yield (0.93%) and y_freeCashflow ($1.94bn) are stale relative to the FY2026 10-K/press-release FCF of $3.1bn (true yield ~1.5%); anyone using the raw quant snapshot without cross-checking primary filings would materially understate FCF
No V1 valuation row exists for STX in v1_valuation_table.csv/v1_valuation.json; v1_verdict set to null and an independent reverse DCF was built instead
STX.confidence_in_thesis: med (operating momentum and guidance-beat pattern are strongly evidenced across three consecutive quarters of primary-source filings; the valuation call rests on a reverse-DCF growth-rate judgement that is inherently uncertain for a historically cyclical hardware name)

valuation_view_vs_v1.reconciliation: No V1 row exists for STX. Independent reverse DCF (FCFF-style, 10y fade to 3% terminal, WACC 9-10%) off the FY2026 record FCF base of $3.1bn implies the 25-Sep-2026 EV of ~$210.3bn requires ~21-24%/yr FCF growth sustained for a full decade - well beyond any multi-year period this cyclical, three-player HDD oligopoly has ever delivered, including its own 2022-2023 down-cycle losses.

ALB.thesis_one_line: The world's largest lithium producer, now genuinely low-debt, riding a real 2026 price recovery that could still swing EBITDA 4-5x on lithium price alone.
kill_criteria: Realized Energy Storage price falls back below $15/kg LCE for two consecutive quarters (vs $19.53/kg in Q2 2026)
Net debt/adjusted EBITDA rises above 1.5x (vs approximately 0.5x at 30 Jun 2026)
Two consecutive quarters of negative adjusted EBITDA in the Energy Storage segment
FY2026 total-corporate scenario table is cut below the ~$10/kg case at any quarterly release
Any further material impairment (Item 2.06 8-K) outside the already-disclosed Ketjen/Eurecat divestitures
key_adverse_facts: Single-commodity (lithium) price exposure: the company's own FY2026 sensitivity table shows adjusted EBITDA ranging from $0.9-1.0bn (2025 avg price) to $4.2-4.4bn (2021-2025 avg price), a 4.5x swing on price alone
Item 2.06 material impairment 8-K (Oct 2025) tied to the Ketjen catalysts divestiture drove a $414.2m Q4 2025 GAAP net loss

7.25% Series A Mandatory Convertible Preferred Stock remains outstanding, a fixed dividend claim and a real dilution overhang (V1's 136.2m if-converted diluted share count vs 118.0m raw shares outstanding)
Q2 2026's 83% OCF conversion was boosted by Talison JV dividend timing and non-recurring working-capital benefits per management's own disclosure, i.e. not fully repeatable at that rate
Trailing GAAP P/E of ~406x is a data-quality artefact of a near-zero prior-year earnings base, not a standalone red flag, but it makes headline P/E screens unreliable for this name
data_conflicts: V1 verdict is 'excessive' (implied 10-year growth 33.4%, base 3y return -1.2%/yr) but this dossier finds V1's ebit_margin_used input (4.27% TTM) is stale, still reflecting the Q3 2025 operating loss; the current run-rate margin (Q2 2026 GAAP operating margin 26.0%) is far higher, which mechanically explains V1's extreme growth requirement

d4/Yahoo enterpriseValue ($15.64bn) is roughly $2.3bn above a directly computed EV from disclosed FY26 balance-sheet figures (market cap + debt - cash approximately $13.3bn), likely because Yahoo's EV includes the mandatory convertible preferred and/or JV minority interests differently than the primary filings suggest
ALB.confidence_in_thesis: med (the pricing recovery and balance-sheet repair are strongly evidenced by primary sources; confidence is capped at medium because the entire thesis is a single-commodity price call that neither this dossier nor the company itself purports to forecast)

valuation_view_vs_v1.reconciliation: V1's reverse DCF holds a stale TTM EBIT margin (4.27%) fixed, which is still dragging in the Q3 2025 operating loss and has not caught up to the Q1-Q2 2026 recovery (16.3% and 26.0% GAAP operating margins respectively); this mechanically inflates the implied-growth requirement to an extreme 33.4%/yr. Using the company's own disclosed FY2026 lithium-price/EBITDA sensitivity table with peer-appropriate EV/EBITDA multiples instead, this dossier estimates bear/base/bull equity values of roughly $54/$126/$282 per share versus the $109.73 close - directionally similar risk asymmetry to V1 but centred closer to fair value than excessive, because the price looks roughly in line with the company's own already-realized run rate rather than requiring a return to the 2021-2025 average price.

CRH.thesis_one_line: The largest US-focused building-materials group, cheap versus peers with 12 straight years of margin gains, now buying the #1 US aggregates position via a debt-funded Arcosa deal.
kill_criteria: Net debt/adjusted EBITDA rises above 3.0x (vs approximately 1.8x today, 2.4x pro forma guided for the Arcosa close)
Arcosa deal fails to close or closes later than the guided Q1 2027 (stockholder vote or regulatory block)
FY2026 guidance (Net income $3.9-4.1bn / Adjusted EBITDA $8.1-8.5bn) is cut at any remaining 2026 release
Adjusted EBITDA margin contracts more than 100bps YoY in any two consecutive quarters
Negative organic (ex-M&A) revenue growth in Americas Materials Solutions for two consecutive quarters
key_adverse_facts: Total debt has risen sharply: $17,653m (FY2025) vs $13,968m (FY2024) vs $11,642m (FY2023), up 26% and 20% YoY respectively, funding a $4.1bn/38-acquisition FY2025 M&A program

Pending $8.5bn all-cash Arcosa acquisition (announced 22 Jun 2026) is funded by committed bridge debt and guides pro forma FY2026E net debt/adjusted EBITDA to 2.4x; deal is not guaranteed to close (Arcosa stockholder approval and regulatory clearance still required, expected close only Q1 2027)

Q1 2026 net loss widened to $176m (vs $94m in Q1 2025), explained by management as higher depreciation/impairment charges and increased interest expense - consistent with rising acquisition-funded debt
12-month share-price momentum is -20.5% despite steady-to-improving fundamentals, i.e. the market has not yet rewarded the value case this dossier makes
No V1 valuation row exists for CRH; the EV/EBITDA-based valuation view in this dossier is independently constructed, not cross-checked against a systematic model
data_conflicts: No V1 valuation row exists for CRH in v1_valuation_table.csv; v1_verdict set to null and an independent EV/EBITDA-based valuation was built instead
CRH.confidence_in_thesis: med-high (the cheap-vs-peer valuation, margin-expansion trend and guidance discipline are strongly evidenced across primary filings; confidence is not higher because the Arcosa deal introduces binary closing risk and the leverage trend is a genuine, not yet fully resolved, watch item)

valuation_view_vs_v1.reconciliation: No V1 row exists for CRH. Independent calculation: market cap ~$56.6bn plus net debt ~$14.9bn gives EV ~$71.5bn, or ~8.6x FY26-guided adjusted EBITDA midpoint ($8.3bn) - below where the closest pure-play aggregates peers (VMC/MLM) typically trade, and the current price does not appear to require growth beyond simply executing the company's own already-reaffirmed FY2026 guidance.
